title: Field LCP at p75 (per form factor)
why: Largest Contentful Paint is a Core Web Vital. web.dev defines good as 2.5 s or less and poor as more than 4 s at the 75th percentile of real Chrome users, per device type. Google uses Core Web Vitals in its page experience signals, without publishing a weight.
fix: Diagnose with the LCP subparts (perf-crux-lcp-subparts) and the lab LCP rules; fix the dominant subpart first.
exemptWhen: CrUX has no data for the URL or origin; the rule is not_evaluated.
thresholds: good <=2500 ms; NI >2500 and <=4000 ms (medium); poor >4000 ms (high) at p75, per form factor
notes: Call CrUX API records:queryRecord with {url, formFactor:'PHONE'} and again with 'DESKTOP' (and the origin as fallback). Read record.metrics.largest_contentful_paint.percentiles.p75 (int ms) and histogram densities. Classify: <=2500 good, 2501-4000 needs improvement, >4000 poor. Severity: poor=high, NI=medium, good=pass. Report PHONE and DESKTOP separately; never average them. If url-level data is missing and the origin is used, state that it is origin data covering all pages. Query strings and fragments are stripped by CrUX normalization (check urlNormalizationDetails). Data is a 28-day rolling window with ~2-day lag, so fixes shipped within the last 28 days are not yet fully reflected.

title: Field INP at p75 (per form factor)
why: Interaction to Next Paint replaced First Input Delay as a Core Web Vital in March 2024. web.dev defines good as 200 ms or less and poor as more than 500 ms at the 75th percentile.
fix: Break up long tasks (scheduler.yield with setTimeout fallback), cut unnecessary JS and third parties, reduce rendering work and DOM size; investigate the Accept handler of consent managers.
exemptWhen: CrUX has too little interaction data to report INP; that is not a failure.
thresholds: good <=200 ms; NI >200 and <=500 ms (medium); poor >500 ms (high) at p75, per form factor
notes: From CrUX queryRecord read metrics.interaction_to_next_paint.percentiles.p75 for PHONE and DESKTOP. Classify <=200 good, 201-500 NI, >500 poor. Severity: poor=high, NI=medium. INP may be absent when there is insufficient interaction data; this is not a failure. Never substitute FID (removed from CrUX Sept 2024). Lab TBT/INP is a proxy only; do not present lab values as the field INP.

title: Field CLS at p75 (per form factor)
why: Cumulative Layout Shift is a Core Web Vital. web.dev defines good as 0.1 or less and poor as more than 0.25 at the 75th percentile. Field CLS covers the whole page lifetime, so it can be worse than lab CLS.
fix: Size images/iframes/ads, reserve space or overlay late-injected UI (cookie banners), use transform animations, tune font fallbacks, keep pages bfcache-eligible.
thresholds: good <=0.1; NI >0.1 and <=0.25 (medium); poor >0.25 (high) at p75, per form factor
notes: From CrUX queryRecord read metrics.cumulative_layout_shift.percentiles.p75 (a 2-decimal STRING; parseFloat). Classify <=0.1 good, >0.1-0.25 NI, >0.25 poor. Severity: poor=high, NI=medium. Field CLS covers the full page lifetime (scroll-triggered shifts, infinite feeds), so a low lab CLS does not refute a poor field CLS. Shifts within 500 ms of discrete input are excluded (hadRecentInput).

title: Core Web Vitals assessment passes in field data (per device type)
why: A page passes the Core Web Vitals assessment when LCP, INP and CLS are all good at the 75th percentile in CrUX. Search Console groups similar URLs, while the CrUX API reports a URL or origin exactly. Google does not publish the ranking weight of the assessment.
fix: Fix the failing metric(s); a page is only as good as its worst Core Web Vital.
exemptWhen: CrUX has no data for the URL or origin; the rule is not_evaluated.
thresholds: Per form factor: pass when LCP and CLS (and INP when it has data) are good at p75; any of them not good = high on PHONE, medium on DESKTOP. Without LCP or CLS data the form factor is not assessable.
notes: Per form factor: if LCP, INP and CLS all have data, pass only if all three p75 values are good. If INP has no data, pass if LCP and CLS are good. If LCP or CLS has no data, result is 'not assessable'. Status of a group = worst metric (Search Console logic). Fail on PHONE = high; fail only on DESKTOP = medium. Search Console groups similar URLs and may show a group status rather than the exact URL; CrUX API is URL- or origin-exact. Never claim a ranking drop magnitude. When only origin-level data exists, say that it covers all pages of the origin.

title: Field data availability and origin fallback labelling
why: CrUX reports data only for public, indexable pages with enough real-user traffic. Knowing whether URL-level, origin-level or no data exists tells the reader how to interpret every field metric.
fix: None needed. Low traffic is not a defect. Use lab data and RUM for pages without field data.
thresholds: URL-level data for any form factor = pass; origin-level data only = info; no data = info, tied to a non-200 status or noindex when either is present.
notes: queryRecord for url per formFactor; on HTTP 404 (no data) retry with origin. Record which level answered. If neither, report 'no field data'. Also query without formFactor to read form_factors fractions. Eligibility needs a public, discoverable page: final status 200 after redirects, no noindex (meta or X-Robots-Tag), and the undisclosed popularity threshold. If the page returns noindex or non-200, absence of CrUX data is expected and must be tied to that finding instead of 'low traffic'. Only Chrome desktop and Android users who opted in to usage statistics and sync contribute; iOS, WebView and Edge are excluded. The 404 response for no data is observed behaviour and is not described on the API page.

title: Field FCP at p75 (supporting metric)
why: First Contentful Paint is a diagnostic metric, not a Core Web Vital. web.dev defines good as 1.8 s or less. It helps explain a slow LCP.
fix: Reduce TTFB and render-blocking CSS/JS; inline critical CSS.
thresholds: good <=1800 ms; NI >1800 and <=3000 ms; poor >3000 ms. NI or poor = low.
notes: metrics.first_contentful_paint.percentiles.p75 per formFactor; classify 1800/3000 ms. FCP is diagnostic, not a Core Web Vital; never report it as a ranking factor. Use it to explain LCP (high FCP plus high LCP means a render-path problem).

title: Field TTFB at p75 (supporting metric)
why: Time to First Byte is a diagnostic metric, not a Core Web Vital. web.dev defines good as 800 ms or less. A slow TTFB delays every later metric, including LCP.
fix: CDN with HTML edge caching, avoid redirects, avoid cache-busting unique query params, reduce server processing, consider 103 Early Hints.
thresholds: good <=800 ms; NI >800 and <=1800 ms; poor >1800 ms at p75. NI or poor = low, or medium when field LCP p75 for the same form factor is not good.
notes: metrics.experimental_time_to_first_byte.percentiles.p75 per formFactor; classify 800/1800 ms. TTFB is not a Core Web Vital: report it as medium only when LCP is NI/poor; otherwise low. Field TTFB includes redirects, service-worker startup, DNS, TCP and TLS, and is collected only on full page loads. 103 Early Hints counts as first bytes in Chrome (responseStart reverted in Chrome 133), so TTFB may look artificially good on sites using it.

title: Field LCP image subparts: dominant bottleneck
why: CrUX splits image LCP into time to first byte, resource load delay, resource load duration and element render delay. web.dev gives guideline shares for each, which point to the bottleneck to fix.
fix: Load delay: make the LCP image discoverable in HTML, add fetchpriority=high, remove lazy loading. Load duration: smaller and modern image formats, CDN. Render delay: cut render-blocking CSS/JS, avoid CSR and anti-flicker hiding. TTFB: server/CDN.
thresholds: Only when LCP p75 >2500 ms: resource load delay >10%, element render delay >10% or TTFB >40% of the sum of the four subpart p75s = medium. Guideline shares, not absolute targets.
notes: Read p75 of largest_contentful_paint_image_time_to_first_byte, _resource_load_delay, _resource_load_duration, _element_render_delay. Compute each as share of their sum. Flag resource_load_delay >10% or element_render_delay >10% of the sum when LCP p75 >2500 ms; flag TTFB share >~40% as server/network-bound. The subparts cover image LCPs only. Each is an independent p75, so they do not add up exactly to LCP p75; describe shares as approximate. web.dev says not to turn the shares into absolute targets. Check largest_contentful_paint_resource_type: when text dominates, the subparts describe a minority of loads.

title: Field LCP resource type mix
why: CrUX reports whether real users' LCP element is mostly an image or text, which decides which optimisations apply.
fix: Use it to choose between image-loading fixes and text/render-path fixes (fonts, CSS, CSR).
thresholds: none
notes: Planned: the CrUX client in src/data/crux.ts keeps percentiles and histograms only, so the fractions of largest_contentful_paint_resource_type are not collected. metrics.largest_contentful_paint_resource_type.fractions (image vs text). Context only.

title: Back/forward navigations not served from bfcache
why: CrUX reports how many back and forward navigations are served from the back/forward cache. web.dev lists bfcache among the most effective improvements, because restored pages load instantly.
fix: Run perf-bfcache-eligibility. Remove unload listeners, avoid no-store when not needed, close open connections on pagehide.
thresholds: back_forward fraction > back_forward_cache fraction AND back_forward + back_forward_cache >= 5% of navigations = low (tool heuristic, not an official threshold)
notes: metrics.navigation_types.fractions: compare back_forward (not restored) with back_forward_cache. Flag when back_forward > back_forward_cache and back_forward + back_forward_cache >= 5% of navigations. Report prerender fraction as context. The 5% gate is a tool heuristic; say so. Some ineligibility reasons are outside the site's control (browser state, extensions).

title: Field metric trend and regressions (History API)
why: The CrUX History API returns weekly 28-day windows, so it shows whether field metrics are improving or regressing over time.
fix: Correlate the regression's start week with deploys and third-party changes.
thresholds: band crossing, or >=20% p75 worsening (tool heuristic)
notes: Planned: the collector does not query records:queryHistoryRecord yet. records:queryHistoryRecord with collectionPeriodCount up to 40 (default 25) per formFactor. Read percentilesTimeseries.p75s. Flag a regression when the latest p75 crosses a threshold band that earlier periods were inside, or worsens >=20% versus the median of the prior 8 periods. Windows are 28 days rolling, updated weekly (Monday ~04:00 UTC), and overlap by 3 weeks. A sudden change takes about 4 weeks to show fully. p75s entries may be null and densities 'NaN' for missing periods; skip them, never treat them as 0. CLS p75s are strings. The API shares the 150 queries/min quota with queryRecord.

title: Users' network RTT context
why: CrUX reports the network round-trip times of real users. They describe the audience's connections, not the server, and help explain field metrics.
fix: With high RTT, favour fewer round trips: CDN, preconnect, fewer critical origins, Early Hints.
thresholds: none: the p75 round-trip time is recorded as context and never fails
notes: metrics.round_trip_time.percentiles.p75 per formFactor. RTT reflects the users' connections, not the server. Never report it as a site defect. It replaced the ECT dimension (removed Sept 2024).

title: Experimental soft-navigation CWV variants (SPAs)
why: CrUX publishes experimental metric variants that include soft navigations in single-page applications. They are not part of the Core Web Vitals assessment.
fix: For SPAs, explains the gap between route-level experience and hard-load CWV.
thresholds: An experimental metric with soft navigations in a different band from its stable metric = info (context). Absent experimental metrics = not applicable.
notes: If present, read experimental_largest_contentful_paint_with_softnavs, experimental_interaction_to_next_paint_with_softnavs and experimental_cumulative_layout_shift_with_softnavs, and compare them with the stable metrics. Experimental (Sept 2026 CrUX release). Never use it for the CWV assessment or present it as what Google ranks on. It combines hard and soft navigations.

title: Lab measurement protocol and variance
why: Lighthouse documents that lab results vary between runs because of network, host load, A/B tests and ads, and recommends the median of several runs. The run protocol and its variance are recorded so that lab numbers can be interpreted.
fix: n/a (methodology). Never run several Lighthouse instances in parallel on one machine.
thresholds: Fewer than 5 valid runs = info; run warnings = info. A coefficient of variation of lab LCP above 15% marks the result unstable (tool heuristic); it needs the per-run values, which the summary does not keep, so only the LCP range is shown.
notes: Run Lighthouse 13.x via the Node API (ESM, Node >=22.19) against a dedicated Chrome. Use mobile (default formFactor 'mobile', throttlingMethod 'simulate', moto g power 2022 UA, 412x823 at DPR 1.75) and desktop config. Do >=5 sequential runs per URL and select the median with computeMedianRun (lighthouse/core/lib/median-run.js). Record lhr.lighthouseVersion, environment.benchmarkIndex and runWarnings. Flag 'unstable' when the LCP numericValue coefficient of variation across runs is >15%. Simulated mobile throttling: 150 ms RTT, ~1.6 Mbps down / 750 Kbps up, 4x CPU slowdown. Desktop uses the desktopDense4G preset (read the exact values from lhr.configSettings). Variance sources: A/B tests, ads, network, host load. Lighthouse docs say the median of 5 runs is twice as stable as 1 run. evidenceLevel is official-other-engine because this is Chrome/Lighthouse documentation, not Search documentation.

title: Lighthouse Performance score (context only)
why: The Lighthouse performance score is a weighted lab summary. Google Search uses field Core Web Vitals, not the Lighthouse score, so the score is context only.
fix: Improve the underlying metrics; do not optimise the score itself.
thresholds: Score 0-49 = info (poor); 50-89 = info (needs improvement); 90-100 = pass. Display bands only; never scored.
notes: lhr.categories.performance.score*100 (median run). Weights: FCP 10, SI 10, LCP 25, TBT 30, CLS 25. Bands 0-49 / 50-89 / 90-100. Must not affect the SEO score. Google's ranking uses CWV field data, not the Lighthouse score. Desktop uses different scoring curves from mobile.

title: Lab LCP (mobile, simulated)
why: Lab LCP from Lighthouse shows the loading path of a first visit on an emulated device. It is a diagnostic: the Core Web Vitals assessment uses field data.
fix: See perf-lcp-* rules.
exemptWhen: CrUX field data exists for the URL or origin; the field result takes precedence and the lab value is reported as a diagnostic only.
thresholds: Lab LCP >4000 ms = medium; >2500 ms = low. When CrUX has field LCP for the lab form factor, a failing lab value is info (diagnostic only).
notes: lhr.audits['largest-contentful-paint'].numericValue (ms) from the median run. Compare with 2500/4000. Lighthouse mobile scoring control points: p10 2500, median 4000 (desktop 1200/2400). Always label it 'lab'. If field data exists, field takes precedence for status. Lab can be worse or better than field (no cache, fixed device, first-visit consent banner, unload of previous page not included).

title: Lab Total Blocking Time (INP risk proxy)
why: Total Blocking Time measures main-thread blocking during load and is the lab proxy for responsiveness. It is not a Core Web Vital, and a navigation run measures no interactions.
fix: Break up long tasks, defer non-critical JS, remove unused JS and third parties.
exemptWhen: CrUX field data exists for the URL or origin; the field result takes precedence and the lab value is reported as a diagnostic only.
thresholds: Lab TBT >600 ms on a mobile run or >350 ms on a desktop run = medium; otherwise pass. When CrUX has field INP for the lab form factor, a failing lab value is info (diagnostic only).
notes: lhr.audits['total-blocking-time'].numericValue. Mobile scoring control points p10 200 ms, median 600 ms (desktop 150/350). Flag >600 ms mobile as heavy main-thread blocking. TBT is not a Core Web Vital and measures load-time blocking only. A navigation-mode Lighthouse run has no INP (the interaction-to-next-paint audit has weight 0 and needs timespan mode). Never call high TBT 'poor INP'.

title: Lab CLS during load
why: Lab CLS covers layout shifts during page load only and is usually lower than field CLS, so a clean lab result does not refute a poor field value.
fix: See perf-cls-culprits.
exemptWhen: CrUX field data exists for the URL or origin; the field result takes precedence and the lab value is reported as a diagnostic only.
thresholds: Lab CLS >0.25 = medium; >0.1 = low. When CrUX has field CLS for the lab form factor, a failing lab value is info (diagnostic only).
notes: lhr.audits['cumulative-layout-shift'].numericValue; compare with 0.1/0.25. Lab CLS covers page load only and is usually lower than field CLS. A clean lab result does not disprove a poor field CLS.

title: LCP image is lazy-loaded
why: web.dev documents that lazy-loading the LCP image delays it until layout is known, which slows LCP. Images in the initial viewport should load eagerly. Lighthouse 13.6 reports this in lcp-discovery-insight.
fix: Remove loading=lazy from images likely in the initial viewport, especially the LCP/hero image; also remove the JS lazy-loader for it.
thresholds: LCP image lazy-loaded without a preload (lcp-discovery-insight eagerlyLoaded false) = high; LCP image URL only in a data-src style attribute of its = high
notes: Identify the LCP element (rendered page: PerformanceObserver 'largest-contentful-paint' entry .element/.url via CDP Runtime.evaluate, or the lcp-discovery-insight checklist). Fail if that has loading='lazy' (and is not preloaded), or if it uses a JS lazy-load pattern (data-src/data-srcset with a placeholder src, 'lazyload' class). Check both mobile and desktop viewports, since the LCP element can differ. A lazy image that is preloaded via passes the insight. web.dev reports 7% of pages hide the LCP image behind data-src.

title: LCP resource not discoverable in initial HTML
why: web.dev documents that an LCP image referenced only from CSS, JavaScript or data attributes cannot be found by the preload scanner, which delays it. Lighthouse 13.6 reports this in lcp-discovery-insight.
fix: Render the hero server-side with src/srcset; for CSS/JS-referenced images add in .
thresholds: lcp-discovery-insight requestDiscoverable false = high; medium when the server HTML references the URL in an , or image preload anyway (conflicting signals). The data-src pattern is reported by perf-lcp-lazy-loaded only.
notes: Take the LCP image URL from the rendered LCP entry. Pass if the raw (non-rendered) HTML contains it in , , or . Fail if it appears only after JS (CSR), only in CSS background-image, or only in data-* attributes. The Lighthouse lcp-discovery-insight check 'Request is discoverable in initial document' requires parser-initiated by the main document, or a link preload. Compare URLs after resolving relative paths and stripping image-CDN width params, otherwise srcset variants produce false fails. Text LCP is out of scope for this rule (see perf-lcp-client-side-rendered). web.dev: 35% of LCP images are not discoverable in the initial HTML.

title: LCP image lacks fetchpriority=high
why: web.dev recommends fetchpriority="high" on the LCP image so the browser requests it before other images. It is a hint, and overusing it removes the benefit.
fix: Add fetchpriority=high to the hero/LCP image only (one or two images max); use fetchpriority=low for hidden carousel slides.
thresholds: Discoverable LCP image without fetchpriority=high (lcp-discovery-insight priorityHinted false) = medium; more than 2 images with fetchpriority=high in the HTML = low (overuse)
notes: For an image LCP that is discoverable, check fetchpriority='high' on the or on its preload link (Lighthouse lcp-discovery-insight: 'fetchpriority=high applied'). Separately count fetchpriority=high on images in raw HTML. It is a hint, not a guarantee. Google Flights LCP went from 2.6 s to 1.9 s. Supported in Chrome/Edge 102, Firefox 132, Safari 17.2. Since Chrome 117 the first 5 large images already get Medium priority. A carousel whose LCP image changes between runs needs care.

title: Lab LCP breakdown dominant phase
why: Lighthouse 13.6 reports lab LCP subparts in lcp-breakdown-insight. The dominant subpart shows whether to fix the server, discovery, download or rendering.
fix: Target the dominant phase (see perf-crux-lcp-subparts).
thresholds: Only when lab LCP >2500 ms and field subparts are absent: resource load delay >10%, element render delay >10% or TTFB >40% of the lab subpart sum = medium (guidelines as perf-crux-lcp-subparts)
notes: Read lhr.audits['lcp-breakdown-insight'] details (TTFB, load delay, load duration, render delay) plus its LCP element node. Report the largest phase and its share of LCP. In Lighthouse 13 the id is lcp-breakdown-insight. It was announced as lcp-breakdown-insight, and the old lcp-breakdown-insight audit was replaced. Text LCP has no load delay/duration. When field subparts exist, prefer them.

title: LCP content depends on client-side rendering
why: web.dev documents that when the LCP content is built by client-side JavaScript, the element render delay grows with script download and execution time.
fix: Server-side render or prerender (SSG) the above-the-fold content; hydrate later.
thresholds: LCP text or image URL absent from the raw HTML and lab LCP > FCP + 500 ms: empty server body = high; otherwise a medium candidate the analyst confirms
notes:
Get the LCP element's text content or image URL from the rendered DOM, then search for it in the raw HTML. Fail if it is missing from the raw HTML (empty app shell such as
) and the LCP time is > FCP + 500 ms in the lab. Normalise whitespace and entities before the text comparison. Personalised or geolocated content can differ legitimately between raw and rendered HTML; the LLM should confirm before reporting.

title: Content hidden by A/B-test anti-flicker or loader
why: web.dev names hiding content while A/B testing or personalisation scripts load as a cause of element render delay for LCP.
fix: Remove the anti-flicker snippet or run experiments server-side/at the edge.
thresholds: A head snippet that hides html or body (opacity 0, visibility hidden, async-hide, known A/B testing pre-hiding) AND lab element render delay >500 ms = medium (tool heuristic). Section-level reveal styles are never matched.
notes: Look in the raw HTML <head> for anti-flicker snippets: inline style setting opacity:0 or visibility:hidden on html/body, an 'async-hide' class, or known optimisation/A-B testing vendor snippets with a timeout. Confirm in the trace that the LCP render delay is large. web.dev names hiding the LCP element while scripts (e.g. A/B libraries) load as a render-delay cause. The 500 ms gate is a heuristic.

title: Render-blocking resources in <head>
why: Synchronous scripts and stylesheets in the head delay the first render. Lighthouse 13.6 reports them in render-blocking-insight, which replaced render-blocking-resources.
fix: Defer or async scripts; inline small critical CSS and load the rest non-blocking; trim CSS size.
exemptWhen: A consent or cookie-blocking script must run synchronously by design; it is reported with that caveat.
thresholds: Parser-blocking external script in the head (no async, defer or type=module) = medium; only synchronous consent scripts = low; otherwise render-blocking-insight failing with an estimated FCP saving above 0 ms = low. A stylesheet without an estimated saving is not a failure.
notes: Raw HTML: in <head>, list <script src> without async/defer/type=module, and <link rel=stylesheet> without a non-matching media query. Lighthouse: lhr.audits['render-blocking-insight'] (score <1 and details items with wasted ms). Legacy id render-blocking-resources no longer exists in Lighthouse 13. Some consent/cookie-blocking scripts must be synchronous by design. Report them with that caveat.

title: Redirects on the document request
why: Each redirect on the document request adds a full round trip before the HTML arrives, which counts in TTFB and LCP. Lighthouse 13.6 reports it in document-latency-insight.
fix: Link internally to final URLs and collapse http->https->www chains into one hop.
exemptWhen: The root URL redirects by country, cookie or language to locale home pages, every locale URL answers 200 when requested directly, and hreflang covers every locale.
The redirect is the http to https or host canonicalisation hop for a URL typed by the user, and internal links use the final URL.
thresholds: Any redirect hop on an audited or linked URL = medium (the cap; the hop count is reported). Exempt: a root locale entry point whose locale URLs answer directly and are covered by hreflang, and an http/https, www or trailing-slash hop for a URL that no audited page links to.
notes: Follow the HTTP chain manually (redirect: 'manual') from the audited/linked URL and count 3xx hops. Lighthouse document-latency-insight check 'noRedirects' fails when redirect duration >0. Redirect time counts in TTFB and LCP. When the user typed the redirecting URL itself, report the chain against internal links and sitemaps that use it, not the canonical page.

title: Slow document server response
why: A slow document response delays everything after it. Lighthouse 13.6 flags server responses above 600 ms in document-latency-insight. One sample from the collector's location is not user TTFB.
fix: Cache HTML at the CDN edge, optimise backend and DB, avoid per-request uncacheable work, use Early Hints for the server think-time.
thresholds: Lab document response (Lighthouse server-response-time) >600 ms = low; medium when the collector sample also exceeds 600 ms. Field TTFB per perf-crux-ttfb-p75.
notes: Measure the document response time (request sent to first byte, excluding DNS/connect) over >=3 warm samples from the HTTP collector; also read document-latency-insight 'serverResponseIsFast'. A single sample from the tool's own location is not user TTFB. Report it as a lab observation with the collector's location.

title: Text resources served without compression
why: HTML, CSS and JavaScript served without gzip, Brotli or zstd take longer to download. Lighthouse 13.6 reports this in document-latency-insight for the document.
fix: Enable Brotli (or zstd) with a gzip fallback at the server/CDN for text MIME types.
thresholds: Uncompressed text HTML >1400 bytes = medium; uncompressed first-party text asset >1400 bytes (referenced resource, or a lab request that transferred at least its decoded size) = low
notes: Request HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, SVG and XML with Accept-Encoding: zstd, br, gzip. Fail when Content-Encoding is missing or not in {gzip, br, zstd, deflate} and the decoded body is >1400 bytes. Lighthouse: document-latency-insight 'usesCompression' (document only). Uncompressed HTML = medium; an uncompressed small asset = low. Brotli vs gzip is a micro-optimisation, so do not flag gzip. Browsers advertise zstd only over HTTPS. Some CDNs compress only when the client advertises an encoding, so always send Accept-Encoding. Do not flag already-compressed types (images, woff2).

title: Static assets served over HTTP/1.1
why: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 multiplex requests over one connection. Lighthouse 13.6 reports origins that serve many static requests over HTTP/1.1 in modern-http-insight.
fix: Enable HTTP/2 (and ideally HTTP/3) at the origin/CDN.
thresholds: First-party origin with >=6 static lab requests and any of them on HTTP/1.x = medium; the same on a third-party origin = low. A missing HTTP/3 is never a failure.
notes: From the CDP Network.responseReceived 'protocol' field (or the Lighthouse modern-http-insight), group static requests by origin. Fail for an origin with >=6 static requests where any request uses HTTP/1.x. Detect HTTP/3 advertisement via the Alt-Svc header containing h3. Node fetch (undici) does not negotiate h2 by default, so take the protocol from the browser, not from the Node HTTP client. Third-party origins are outside the site's control; report them separately. A missing HTTP/3 is not a defect.

title: Static assets with short or missing cache lifetime
why: Static assets with a short or missing cache lifetime are downloaded again on repeat visits. Lighthouse 13.6 reports this in cache-insight. The benefit applies to repeat visits only.
fix: Fingerprint asset filenames and serve them with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable (immutable is optional); serve HTML with no-cache plus an ETag.
exemptWhen: The assets belong to third parties outside the site's control.
thresholds: Any first-party static resource listed by cache-insight (TTL missing or <30 d) = low; fingerprinted file names among them are named. Third-party resources never fail.
notes: For static resources (script, stylesheet, image, font, media) with cacheable status: compute TTL from max-age, else Expires. Flag missing TTL or TTL <30 days unless no-store/no-cache/must-revalidate/private is set (Lighthouse cache-insight logic). Separately, for fingerprinted filenames (hash in the path, e.g. app.3f9a1c.js) expect max-age >= 31536000. The legacy id cache-insight is gone; use cache-insight. Repeat-visit benefit only, so low severity. Third-party assets (analytics) are not under the site's control. max-age=0 is intentionally ignored by the insight.

title: HTML served with Cache-Control: no-store
why: Cache-Control: no-store on HTML prevents caching and, in browsers other than recent Chrome, keeps the page out of the back/forward cache. It is appropriate for personalised or private pages.
fix: Use no-cache or max-age=0 for freshness unless the page contains sensitive data.
exemptWhen: The page is personalised, behind login, or a private redirect.
The HTML is served with max-age=0 or no-cache plus an ETag or Last-Modified from a CDN edge cache; that is revalidation, not missing caching.
thresholds: no-store on a 200, indexable HTML response without private, a password field or Set-Cookie = low; with Set-Cookie = low candidate the analyst confirms
notes: Document response Cache-Control contains no-store on a page with no evident authenticated or sensitive content (no Set-Cookie session, public crawlable page). Since a 100% rollout in Mar-Apr 2025, Chrome admits most no-store pages to bfcache. It evicts them on cookie changes and after 3 min (10 min for other pages), and keeps them out when the page uses WebSocket, WebTransport or WebRTC. Other browsers may still block bfcache. Do not claim 'no-store blocks bfcache in Chrome'.

title: Page not eligible for the back/forward cache
why: web.dev lists the back/forward cache among the most effective improvements for LCP and CLS on history navigations. Lighthouse 13.6 tests eligibility in the bf-cache audit.
fix: Remove unload handlers, avoid unnecessary no-store, close IndexedDB/WebSocket/fetch on pagehide, avoid window.opener (use noopener).
exemptWhen: The only reasons reported come from automation or browser-internal conditions.
thresholds: Any actionable (PageSupportNeeded) bf-cache reason not caused by the automated run = medium
notes: Lighthouse lhr.audits['bf-cache'] (score 0 means failures; details list reasons and failure types). Alternatively, via CDP: navigate A->B->back and listen for Page.backForwardCacheNotUsed (notRestoredExplanations with type PageSupportNeeded / SupportPending / Circumstantial). web.dev lists bfcache among the top recommendations for LCP and CLS. Report only actionable reasons; reasons from headless or automation conditions and browser-internal reasons are not site defects. A restored page resets CLS to 0.

title: unload event listeners present
why: unload listeners keep pages out of the back/forward cache in some browsers. Chrome has deprecated unload, so the remaining impact is mainly in other browsers.
fix: Replace with pagehide/visibilitychange. Optionally send Permissions-Policy: unload=() (Chromium only).
thresholds: Any unload listener in an inline script or body onunload (server HTML or rendered page), or an unload reason in bf-cache = low. External script files are not read.
notes: Lighthouse best-practices audit no-unload-listeners if present. Otherwise use CDP DOMDebugger.getEventListeners on window for type 'unload', and search script sources for addEventListener('unload' / window.onunload. Chrome finished deprecating unload across all page loads in 2026. It no longer fires by default unless the site opts back in via Permissions-Policy, and it can still fire on iOS (WebKit). The impact is now mainly Firefox bfcache ineligibility, so low severity. Third-party scripts often add these listeners. Lighthouse 13.6 has no unload-listener audit; detect listeners from the page.

title: Images without explicit dimensions
why: web.dev documents that images without width and height attributes (or an aspect-ratio) cause layout shifts when they load. Lighthouse 13.6 reports them in the unsized-images audit.
fix: Add width and height attributes (keep the same aspect ratio across srcset candidates) or set aspect-ratio in CSS.
exemptWhen: CSS sets both dimensions or an aspect-ratio for the image.
thresholds: Any unsized image (Lighthouse unsized-images, which accounts for CSS sizing) in the first viewport of the lab run = medium; only below it = low
notes: Lighthouse unsized-images audit (diagnostic, still in LH13). Raw/rendered DOM: lacking either width+height attributes or CSS width+height/aspect-ratio, excluding position:fixed/absolute, inline SVG and images with an explicitly sized container. 66% of pages have at least one unsized image (web.dev). width/height with CSS height:auto is correct. Do not flag images where CSS sets both dimensions.

title: Layout shift culprits during load
why: Lighthouse 13.6 attributes layout shifts to causes such as unsized media, injected content and web fonts in cls-culprits-insight. The shifted element is often not the cause.
fix: Fix the cause named by the insight: dimensions, reserved space, font fallback metrics, transform animations.
thresholds: Worst shift cluster >0.05 (tool heuristic): >=0.1 = medium, otherwise low. Without a root cause attributed by Lighthouse the finding is a candidate the analyst confirms.
notes: lhr.audits['cls-culprits-insight'] details: shift clusters with root causes (unsized images, web fonts, injected iframes/content, non-composited animations). Rendered page: PerformanceObserver 'layout-shift' entries with sources[].node, excluding hadRecentInput. The shifted element is often not the cause (web.dev). The LLM must name the cause, not the moved node. The 0.05 candidate cut-off is a tool heuristic.

title: Banners or consent notices inserted into the page flow shift content
why: web.dev documents that cookie notices and banners inserted into the document flow after load shift content and can become the LCP element. Overlays positioned over the content do not shift it.
fix: Render the banner as an overlay (fixed/sticky footer or modal) or reserve its space in the server HTML.
exemptWhen: The banner is a fixed or sticky overlay that does not move content.
thresholds: shift caused by an in-flow inserted banner = fail
notes: Planned: the rendered facts record neither when a node was inserted nor its computed position, so an in-flow injected banner cannot be told from a fixed overlay. Rendered page: find consent, promo or app banners (fixed/sticky vs static positioning) inserted after first paint. A static, in-flow banner at the top that coincides with a layout-shift entry whose sources include main content = fail. Lab runs see a first-time visitor (banner shown). Field users who already consented do not, so impact is overstated in the lab.

title: Ads, iframes and embeds without reserved space
why: web.dev recommends reserving space for ads, iframes and embeds, because content that loads into unsized containers shifts the page.
fix: Reserve the most likely size with min-height/aspect-ratio; keep the placeholder when no ad fills; place dynamic slots lower in the viewport.
thresholds: Embed without width and height attributes or an inline height or aspect-ratio, with an injected-iframe shift attributed by Lighthouse = medium; without an attributed shift = low candidate the analyst confirms (a stylesheet may reserve the space)
notes: Rendered DOM: iframes, ad slots (common ad containers), video embeds and social embeds without width/height, aspect-ratio or min-height on the element or its container; confirm with layout-shift sources. Shifts inside cross-origin iframes are not measurable by web APIs.

title: Animations of layout-inducing properties
why: Animations of layout-inducing properties such as top, margin or width run on the main thread and can cause layout shifts. Lighthouse 13.6 reports them in non-composited-animations.
fix: Animate transform/opacity instead; respect prefers-reduced-motion.
thresholds: Any non-composited animation reported by Lighthouse = low
notes: Lighthouse non-composited-animations audit (diagnostic). CSS scan of @keyframes/transitions animating top/left/right/bottom/margin/width/height/border. web.dev: pages animating layout-inducing properties are 15% less likely to have good CLS, and margin/border animations show nearly 2x the poor-CLS rate. Animations among the shift causes are reported by perf-cls-culprits.

title: Web fonts block text rendering
why: Web fonts without font-display: swap or optional hide text until the font loads. Lighthouse 13.6 reports this in font-display-insight.
fix: Use font-display: swap for branding/headlines and optional for body text; add size-adjust/metric overrides to the fallback to cut CLS.
thresholds: font-display-insight failing with wasted time on any font = low
notes: Lighthouse font-display-insight score <1. CSS: @font-face without font-display, or with auto/block, for fonts used above the fold. Icon fonts with swap cause shifts; prefer SVG icons. Google Fonts URLs accept &display=swap.

title: Font preload or preconnect missing crossorigin
why: Fonts are fetched in CORS mode, so a preload or preconnect for a font without the crossorigin attribute is not reused and the font is downloaded twice.
fix: Add crossorigin (anonymous) to font preloads and to the font-origin preconnect.
thresholds: Any font preload without crossorigin, or a preconnect to a font-file origin without crossorigin and without a CORS twin = low
notes: Raw HTML: <link rel=preload as=font> without a crossorigin attribute; <link rel=preconnect> to a font-file origin (e.g. fonts.gstatic.com) without crossorigin. Without it the preload is not reused (double fetch) and the preconnect only does DNS.

title: Fonts not served as WOFF2 / excessive font files
why: WOFF2 is the smallest widely supported font format, and many font files on the initial load compete with critical resources.
fix: Serve WOFF2 only, subset with unicode-range, use fewer families/weights or a variable font where it saves bytes.
exemptWhen: Reported as an optimisation opportunity, not a defect, unless the resource is on the LCP path.
thresholds: Any non-woff2 font file in the lab load = low; more than 6 font files = low (tool heuristic)
notes: Network log: font requests whose Content-Type or extension is not woff2; count font files and bytes on the page. Micro-optimisation unless fonts sit on the LCP path. The 6-file cut-off is heuristic.

title: Preconnect hint hygiene
why: web.dev recommends preconnect only for origins that are used early, because unused connections are closed after about 10 seconds and too many hints compete with each other.
fix: Preconnect only to the 1-3 critical origins used early; use dns-prefetch for others in a separate <link>.
thresholds: Each = low: more than 4 preconnects (heuristic); preconnect combined with dns-prefetch in one rel; a preconnected origin without a lab request in the first 10 s; an origin Lighthouse estimates a preconnect would speed up
notes: Raw HTML <link rel=preconnect>: (a) count; (b) preconnected origins that get no request in the first 10 s of the lab load; (c) rel='preconnect dns-prefetch' combined in one tag; (d) critical third-party origins on the LCP path without a preconnect (from network-dependency-tree-insight). No official numeric limit exists ('limit the number'). The >4 warning is a heuristic and must be phrased that way. The browser closes unused connections after 10 s.

title: Deep critical request chains
why: Long chains of dependent requests on the critical path delay the first render and LCP. Lighthouse 13.6 reports them in network-dependency-tree-insight, which replaced critical-request-chains and network-dependency-tree-insight.
fix: Flatten chains (CSS @import, JS-loaded CSS/fonts), preload late-discovered critical resources.
thresholds: Deepest critical request chain more than 3 requests after the document = low (tool heuristic). The insight fails on any two-request chain, so its score alone is not used.
notes: lhr.audits['network-dependency-tree-insight'] details: maximum critical path latency and chain depth. Replaces the legacy critical-request-chains and network-dependency-tree-insight audits. The depth cut-off is a heuristic.

title: Images are delivered at an efficient size and format
why: Lighthouse 13.6 reports oversized, uncompressed or legacy-format images in image-delivery-insight. Google Images guidance also recommends responsive images with srcset and an img fallback. The impact is largest on the LCP image.
fix: Serve responsive srcset/sizes, AVIF/WebP, sensible quality; replace animated GIFs with video.
thresholds: LCP image with savings >=10 KiB = medium; other images, total savings >=100 KiB = low (heuristic)
notes: lhr.audits['image-delivery-insight'] items (oversized for display size, legacy format, poor compression, animated GIF): sum the estimated savings. Rendered DOM: images whose intrinsic width >2x rendered width x DPR; large images without srcset/sizes. Most material when it is the LCP image (load duration subpart). Replaces uses-webp-images, uses-optimized-images, image-delivery-insight and efficient-animated-content.

title: Below-the-fold images loaded eagerly
why: Images below the initial viewport that load eagerly compete with critical resources. Lighthouse 13 removed its offscreen-images audit, so the tool computes this itself.
fix: Add loading=lazy (with width/height) to images and iframes outside the first viewport.
exemptWhen: The same image appears more than once on a page; that is not a duplicate-content or duplicate-image problem.
thresholds: >=5 such images or >=200 KiB = flag (heuristic)
notes: Planned: the rendered facts keep no image positions or request start times, so images more than 1.5 viewports below the fold cannot be located. Rendered DOM at the mobile viewport: /

title: Lab interaction latency (scripted)
why: Scripted interactions in a Lighthouse timespan run measure lab interaction latency, reported in inp-breakdown-insight. It is a risk indicator, not field INP.
fix: Yield inside handlers (scheduler.yield, fallback setTimeout), defer non-visual work, reduce DOM/style work, and ask the CMP whether it yields after Accept.
thresholds: interaction >200 ms = flag; >500 ms = higher risk (still capped at medium)
notes: Lighthouse user flow timespan, or CDP: click the primary UI controls (menu toggle, accordion, consent Accept, add-to-cart), read the Event Timing entries and inp-breakdown-insight (input delay, processing duration, presentation delay). A lab result on emulated CPU is not field INP. Phrase it as 'risk' unless CrUX INP agrees. Headless runs without interactions produce no INP at all. Planned: needs scripted interactions in timespan mode, which v1 does not run.

title: Long main-thread tasks during load
why: Main-thread tasks longer than 50 ms block input handling and rendering. web.dev documents breaking them up to improve responsiveness.
fix: Split work and yield; code-split; defer hydration of below-the-fold components; remove dead tags.
thresholds: Sum of (task - 50 ms) over the long tasks Lighthouse lists >600 ms = medium (Lighthouse lists at most 20 tasks, so the sum is a lower bound; applied to mobile and desktop runs)
notes: Lighthouse long-tasks, mainthread-work-breakdown and bootup-time audits. Count tasks >50 ms, total blocking ms, and the top scripts by execution time (attribute to first party vs third party). Hydration of large SSR frameworks commonly shows as long tasks. The LLM may name the framework only when bundle or script evidence identifies it. isInputPending is no longer recommended.

title: Forced synchronous layout (layout thrashing)
why: Reading layout properties after changing styles forces synchronous layout. Lighthouse 13.6 reports it in forced-reflow-insight.
fix: Batch DOM reads before writes; avoid reading layout properties right after mutations.
thresholds: forced-reflow-insight failing = low
notes: lhr.audits['forced-reflow-insight'] score <1; list top call sites.

title: Large DOM / expensive style and layout
why: Large DOMs make style calculation and layout slower, which affects responsiveness. Lighthouse 13.6 reports this in dom-size-insight.
fix: Remove hidden duplicate markup (e.g. separate mobile/desktop menus), paginate/virtualise long lists, use content-visibility:auto for off-screen sections.
thresholds: More than 1400 rendered elements, or dom-size-insight informative (costly layout or style recalculation) = low; 801-1400 elements = info (legacy Lighthouse warning)
notes: Element count of the rendered DOM (document.getElementsByTagName('*').length) and max depth. Lighthouse dom-size-insight: informative when layout events with >100 dirty objects or style recalcs with >300 elements took >=40 ms. The 800/1400 counts come from the legacy dom-size audit cited by web.dev. The LH13 insight has no element-count fail state.

title: Third-party and tag-manager scripts cost main-thread time and bytes
why: Lighthouse 13.6 attributes main-thread time and transfer size to third-party entities in third-parties-insight. Heavy third-party scripts slow loading and responsiveness.
fix: Prune unused tag-manager tags, load non-critical third parties after interaction or idle, self-host or preconnect the CMP, use facades for heavy embeds.
exemptWhen: The script is a legally required consent manager; the recommendation is optimisation, not removal.
Analytics or tag-manager scripts are absent from the raw and initial rendered HTML because they are injected only after consent.
thresholds: Third-party entity with >=250 ms lab main-thread time = medium; >=100 KiB only = low; only consent managers = low (optimisation, not removal). Cut-offs are heuristics.
notes: lhr.audits['third-parties-insight']: per entity transfer size and main-thread time. Flag entities with main-thread time >=250 ms or >=100 KiB on mobile. Classify tag managers, consent managers, chat widgets, A/B testing, ads and analytics. The cut-offs are heuristics. A consent manager may be legally required, so recommend optimisation, not removal.

title: Heavy embeds loaded eagerly (facade candidates)
why: Heavy embeds such as video players and chat widgets can be replaced by a lightweight facade that loads the embed on interaction. Lighthouse 13 removed its facade audit, so the tool computes this itself.
fix: Use a facade (e.g. lite-youtube-embed, a chat loader) that loads the real embed on click.
thresholds: Video or chat embed loaded before any interaction costing >=100 KiB or >=100 ms main thread in the lab load = low (heuristic)
notes: Rendered DOM/network: YouTube/Vimeo iframes, chat widgets (Intercom, Drift, HubSpot chat, Messenger, etc.) and social widgets loaded before any interaction; sum their bytes and main-thread time. The third-party-facades audit was removed in Lighthouse 13; compute it yourself. Facades can lose features such as chat unread badges.

title: Unused JavaScript and CSS
why: Lighthouse 13.6 reports JavaScript and CSS downloaded but unused during load in unused-javascript and unused-css-rules. Code used later in the session also counts as unused.
fix: Code-split by route, drop unused libraries, purge unused CSS, remove stale tags.
thresholds: Unused JS >=150 KiB = low; unused CSS >=50 KiB = low (heuristics, one load without interactions)
notes: Lighthouse unused-javascript and unused-css-rules audits: details.overallSavingsBytes and per-URL wasted bytes. Coverage reflects one page load without interactions, so code used later counts as 'unused'. Never promise the savings.

title: Legacy polyfills and duplicated modules
why: Lighthouse 13.6 reports polyfills for features modern browsers support in legacy-javascript-insight and modules bundled twice in duplicated-javascript-insight.
fix: Target Baseline browsers in the bundler and dedupe dependencies.
thresholds: legacy-javascript-insight or duplicated-javascript-insight failing = low
notes: lhr.audits['legacy-javascript-insight'] and ['duplicated-javascript-insight'] wasted bytes. Micro-optimisation.

title: Unminified CSS/JS
why: Lighthouse 13.6 reports CSS and JavaScript that could be smaller when minified in unminified-css and unminified-javascript. Compression already removes most of the difference.
fix: Enable minification in the build.
thresholds: unminified-css plus unminified-javascript savings >=10 KiB = low
notes: Lighthouse unminified-css and unminified-javascript wasted bytes. Micro-optimisation; compression already removes most of the gap.

title: Total page weight and request count
why: Lighthouse 13.6 flags pages above about 4 MB in total-byte-weight. Weight alone is not a ranking factor; bytes on the critical path matter most.
fix: Find the largest contributors (images, video, JS) and address them through the specific rules.
thresholds: >4000 KiB = low; >2667 KiB = info
notes: lhr.audits['total-byte-weight'].numericValue (bytes) and the request count from the network log. Lighthouse scoring control points: p10 2667 KiB, median 4000 KiB. Weight alone is not a ranking factor. Only bytes on the critical path matter for LCP.

title: Instant navigations via speculation rules
why: Chrome supports speculation rules that prefetch or prerender likely next pages for near-instant navigation. Their absence is not a defect; rules that match state-changing URLs are.
fix: Consider document rules with moderate eagerness for likely next pages; exclude logout and state-changing links; handle analytics on activation.
thresholds: Absence is not a defect (not applicable). A prefetch or prerender rule that lists or matches a state-changing link on the page (logout, cart, checkout) = info; invalid JSON = info. Conditions that need the DOM (selector_matches) are not decided.
notes: Raw HTML <script type=speculationrules> or a Speculation-Rules response header. Parse the JSON: prerender/prefetch, eagerness, and where/href_matches exclusions (logout, cart, ?add-to-cart). Chrome-only (Firefox/Safari limited or behind flags). Chrome limits: moderate/eager on desktop 2 prefetch/2 prerender (FIFO); immediate 50/10. Speculations are suppressed under Save-Data or low memory. Absence is not a defect.

title: 103 Early Hints opportunity
why: 103 Early Hints let a server send preconnect and preload hints while it prepares a slow response. It helps only when the server response is slow.
fix: Send 103 with preconnect/preload for critical CSS, fonts and the hero image over HTTP/2+, only for sec-fetch-mode: navigate.
thresholds: slow server response and no 103 = info
notes: Planned: the HTTP client does not record 103 informational responses. Inspect the document response for a 103 status (requires a raw HTTP/2 client or CDP) and its Link headers. When field or lab TTFB >600 ms and none is sent, mark it as an opportunity. Chrome supports only preconnect and preload. Safari supports preconnect only. Hints are dropped on cross-origin redirects. Useless when the server answers 200 immediately.

title: HTML not served from a CDN/edge cache
why: Serving HTML from a CDN or edge cache shortens TTFB for distant users. Detection relies on response headers and is heuristic, so the rule says no CDN markers were detected rather than that no CDN exists.
fix: Serve through a CDN; cache static or anonymous HTML briefly at the edge; avoid unique query params that bypass the cache.
exemptWhen: The HTML is served with max-age=0 or no-cache plus an ETag or Last-Modified from a CDN edge cache; that is revalidation, not missing caching.
thresholds: No CDN markers detected on any audited HTML response = info; markers present = pass. It is reported as no markers detected, never as no CDN.
notes: Document response headers: CDN markers (cf-cache-status, x-cache, x-served-by, age, via, server values of known CDNs, x-vercel-cache, etc.). Record HIT/MISS across 2 consecutive requests. Header-based CDN detection is heuristic, and some CDNs strip their markers. Never report 'no CDN' as fact; say 'no CDN markers detected'. Only 33% of HTML requests are served from a CDN (Web Almanac, via web.dev).

title: Consent banner affects lab measurements
why: Lighthouse measures a first-time visitor who always sees the consent banner, while field data mixes new and returning users. When the LCP element is in the consent UI, the lab LCP is annotated.
fix: If the banner is the LCP element on mobile, make it smaller or render it server-side early; test the accepted state with a cookie header too.
thresholds: Lab LCP element inside a consent dialog = info (annotates the lab LCP)
notes: Detect a consent dialog in the rendered DOM (common CMP containers/roles). Check whether the lab LCP element sits inside it. Lighthouse and PSI measure a first-time visitor (PSI sets no cookies). Field data mixes consented and new users. The LLM must not extrapolate lab banner effects to field metrics.
